classification.difficultyReason: The hint supplies the triangle criterion and square representation; the remaining demand is expressing ordered break-point lengths as inequalities and finding both symmetric favourable regions.

content.prompt:
If you break a stick at two points chosen uniformly, find the probability that the three resulting sticks can be used to form a triangle.

Hint: Recall that three lengths can form a triangle if and only if no individual piece is at least half the total length. Try representing the two break points on a unit square to visualise the condition geometrically.

answer.short:
$\frac14$.

Represent the two break points on a unit square; the favourable region consists of two triangles of total area $\frac14$.
answer.worked:
Take the stick to have length $1$, with independently chosen break points $x,y\in[0,1]$. Their sample space is a unit square.

When $x<y$, the piece lengths are $x$, $y-x$ and $1-y$. All three must be less than $\frac12$, so
$$\begin{align*}x&<\frac12,\\y&>\frac12,\\y-x&<\frac12.\end{align*}$$
These inequalities describe the triangle with vertices $(0,\frac12)$, $(\frac12,\frac12)$ and $(\frac12,1)$. The case $y<x$ gives its reflection in $y=x$.

Each favourable triangle has perpendicular sides of length $\frac12$. Therefore,
$$\begin{align*}\Pr(\text{triangle})&=\frac{2\left(\frac12\times\frac12\times\frac12\right)}{1}\\\Pr(\text{triangle})&=\frac14.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored unit-square solution with the two favourable triangles labelled E_1 and E_2. Outlines describe limiting boundaries; boundaries have probability zero.
spec.mathematics: For x<y: x<1/2, y>1/2 and y-x<1/2. Reflect across y=x for y<x. Each region has area 1/8.
